title: Organization of texture segregation processing in primate visual cortex.
abstract: We investigated the intracortical organization of neuronal mass activity that is related to texture segregation on the basis of orientation contrast. Evoked potentials were recorded to a stimulus, signalling a contribution from texture segregation-sensitive mechanisms by means of specific response components. The specific components could only be recorded when textons had a spatial organization that leads to the percept of image segmentation. Equivalent dipole estimations of the specific response components suggested the presence of texture segregation-related activity in the primary visual cortex. These results were corroborated by current-source-density analysis of intracortical recordings in the awake monkey. A specific involvement of layers 2/3 and 5 of area 17 in the global process of image segmentation could be demonstrated.
